app_documentation:
BloomDash is a flower delivery application for web (React), iOS and Android (React Native), backed by a Node.js REST API and a PostgreSQL database. It lets customers browse a photo-first catalog of flowers and bouquets, order them online with a chosen delivery date and address, and follow each delivery from preparation to their door. Its purpose is to make sending flowers fast and reliable. A first-time customer should be able to complete an order in under 5 minutes, and the florist's inventory and courier operations are managed in the same system.

The MVP has five features. F1 Flower Catalog Browsing (High) offers search and filtering by category, price and occasion, with photos, prices and availability; out-of-stock items are marked unavailable and cannot be added to the cart. F2 Cart and Order Placement (High) covers the cart, delivery date and address selection, and secure Stripe payment with an order confirmation; if payment fails, no order is created and the customer sees an error with a retry option. F3 Delivery Tracking (High) shows real-time order status, with a live Google Maps courier view, an ETA card and a status timeline. Status changes reach the customer within 30 seconds through Firebase Cloud Messaging push notifications or polling, and couriers can mark orders delivered, which notifies the customer and closes the order. F4 User Accounts and Order History (Medium) provides registration and login, saved addresses, past orders and one-tap reorder at current prices. F5 Admin Catalog and Order Management (Medium) lets florist staff add, edit and remove products, update prices and stock, view paid orders and assign them to couriers.

The intended users are three roles: Customers, who browse, order, pay and track; Couriers, who see assigned deliveries and update their status; and Admins (florist staff), who manage inventory, orders and courier assignment. The design is a warm, editorial look with a rose primary color (#D6336C), green secondary, Playfair Display headings and Inter body text, bottom navigation (Home, Search, Orders, Profile), 44px minimum touch targets and WCAG AA accessibility. The seven designed screens are Home & Catalog, Product Details, Cart & Checkout, Order Tracking, Account & Order History, and the Admin & Courier Console.

The non-functional requirements are: catalog pages load in under 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; all traffic uses HTTPS, passwords are hashed with bcrypt and card data is handled only by PCI-DSS compliant Stripe; monthly uptime is 99.5% excluding scheduled maintenance; and customer addresses and contact data are encrypted at rest and purged within 30 days of an account deletion request. The database has 19 tables, including users with roles, addresses, products with categories, occasions and images, carts, orders with address and price snapshots, payments, deliveries, status history and notifications. The delivery plan has 15 tasks (T1-T15) from design system and schema through API, screens, payments, tracking, history, admin and courier consoles, and a final performance, usability and accessibility QA pass with a staging release. Key risks to monitor are team capacity across three platforms, Stripe integration and failure handling, real-time tracking quotas, privacy requirements deferred past T2, and delays from app store review and third-party API setup.

glossary.Bouquet: A pre-arranged set of flowers sold as a single catalog product in BloomDash, which customers can filter by category, price and occasion.
glossary.Order Status: The stage of an order in its lifecycle (paid, preparing, ready_for_delivery, out_for_delivery, delivered, cancelled). Customers see changes within 30 seconds.
glossary.Courier: A user role for delivery staff who see assigned deliveries, update delivery status and mark orders as delivered.
glossary.Admin: A florist staff user role who manages products, stock and prices, views incoming paid orders and assigns them to couriers.
glossary.Payment Intent: A Stripe object representing a payment attempt. BloomDash stores only its ID, never card data, and creates an order only after payment succeeds.
glossary.Reorder: A feature that adds the items from a past order to the cart at current product prices, rather than the prices from the original purchase.
